reference.description: The verse or passage he was copying, as the app names it: 'John 1:1', 'Genesis 1:1', 'Romans 8:1-4'.

language.description: The language of the text he copied: 'en' English, 'grc' Koine Greek (with its accents and breathings), 'hbo' Biblical Hebrew (pointed: letters and vowel points, no cantillation marks).

mode.description: 'copywork' (the default, left out) when he copied the text from sight; 'dictation' when the app read the text to him a phrase at a time with the text hidden and he wrote it from hearing it. The page is judged against `words` in both; a dictated page also has words that sound like the model's written wrongly.

words.description: The model text, split on spaces into its words, exactly as the app showed it to him to copy (or, in a dictation, as the app read it to him and now shows it): English words keep their punctuation and capital letters; Greek words are NFC with their accents and breathings; Hebrew words are pointed. The answer marks these words one for one, in this order.
